title: Methods for Identification of the Opportunistic Gut Mycobiome from Colorectal Adenocarcinoma Biopsy Tissues
author: Yunus, Mokhtar, et al.
materials:
A. Pre-treatment of tissue biopsy samples
•Tissue biopsies were sampled and transported under conditions that avoided contamination.•180 µL of buffer PKB (Kit 1) was pipetted into a sample tube (Kit 1).•The sample was transferred to sterile support, e.g., a petri dish, and cut into small pieces (∼0.5 × 0.5 cm) using a sterile scalpel.•The cut sample was then transferred to the sample tube filled with buffer PKB, and 20 µL of Proteinase K (Kit 2) was added.•The mixture was vortexed for 15 s and incubated for 1 hour at 56 °C and 1000 rpm using a thermomixer.•The transport solution was filled up to 1 mL if available, or with buffer TSB, using the measuring line of the tube.

was added to the sample, followed by 1.4 µL of β-mercaptoethanol (Kit 2).•The sample was vortexed for 15 s, and incubated at 37 °C for 30 min with shaking at 1000 rpm using a thermomixer.•The sample was briefly centrifuged and 150 µL of buffer RP was added.•20 µL of Proteinase K (Kit

was added and vortexed for 15 s.•The sample was incubated at 56 °C for 10 min, with shaking at 1000 rpm using a thermomixer.•The sample was briefly centrifuged.•250 µL of buffer CS was added and vortexed for 15 s, then briefly centrifuged.•250 µL of buffer AB was added and vortexed for 15 s, then briefly centrifuged again to clear the lid.•The lysate was then pipetted into a spin column, taking precautions to prevent the transfer of any particles that remain unresolved.•The spin column was then centrifuged at a minimum speed of 12,000xg for 30 to 60 s.•The column was then removed and placed in a new 2 mL collection tube.•400 µL of buffer WB was added and the spin column was centrifuged again at a minimum speed of 12,000xg for 30 to 60 s.•The column was removed again and placed in a new 2 mL collection tube.•400 µL of 70% Ethanol was added and the spin column was centrifuged at a minimum speed of 12,000xg for 3 min.•The column was carefully removed and placed in a 1.5 mL elution tube.•30 µL of deionized water, heated to 70 °C, was added to the column.•The sample was incubated at room temperature for 1 min before centrifuging at a minimum speed of 12,000xg for 1 min.•The column was discarded, the lid of the elution tube was closed, and the column was discarded.•The eluted DNA was ready to be analyzed, or stored at −80 °C.

The barcoded amplicons obtained in the preceding stages were visualized using gel electrophoresis and were then aggregated based on the intensity of their respective bands. The aggregated amplicons were then subjected to DNA purification utilizing SPRI beads at a 0.8 X (v/v) ratio. The NEB Ultra II Library Preparation Kit (New England Biolabs, USA) was employed to process the purified pooled amplicons. The expected fragment size was confirmed, and the Promega Glomax reagent was used to quantify the libraries. In instances where some libraries exhibited a low yield, two distinct library pools with a ratio of samples were constructed to mitigate this. The final library pool's concentration was determined using Denovix high-sensitivity assay. The amplicon libraries and two controls were subsequently sequenced using a 2 × 150 bp configuration on an Illumina NovaSEQ6000 (Illumina, San Diego, CA) platform.

steps.title: Pre‑treat tissue biopsies
steps.instruction: Transport biopsies under sterile, contamination‑free conditions, place each sample on a sterile petri dish, cut into ~0.5 × 0.5 cm pieces with a sterile scalpel, and transfer the pieces into a kit tube containing 180 µL buffer PKB (Kit 1).

steps.title: Proteinase K digestion
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL Proteinase K (Kit 2) to the tube, vortex 15 s, then incubate 1 h at 56 °C with shaking at 1000 rpm in a thermomixer; if the transport solution volume is <1 mL, bring to 1 mL with buffer TSB using the tube’s measuring line.

steps.title: DNA extraction – first wash
steps.instruction: Add 250 µL buffer CM, vortex 15 s, let stand 5 min at room temperature (18‑25 °C), briefly centrifuge, then add 250 µL buffer DB1.

steps.title: DNase treatment
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL MolDNase B (Kit 2), vortex 15 s, incubate 15 min at room temperature, then centrifuge ≥12 000 × g for 10 min.

steps.title: Pellet washing and resuspension
steps.instruction: Discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 1 mL buffer RS, centrifuge ≥12 000 × g for 5 min, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 80 µL buffer RL, briefly centrifuge.

steps.title: Cell lysis and reduction
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL BugLysis (Kit 2) and 1.4 µL β‑mercaptoethanol (Kit 2), vortex 15 s, incubate 30 min at 37 °C with shaking at 1000 rpm, briefly centrifuge.

steps.title: Proteinase K digestion (second)
steps.instruction: Add 150 µL buffer RP, then 20 µL Proteinase K (Kit 2), vortex 15 s, incubate 10 min at 56 °C with shaking at 1000 rpm, briefly centrifuge.

steps.title: Lysis buffer addition
steps.instruction: Add 250 µL buffer CS, vortex 15 s, briefly centrifuge; then add 250 µL buffer AB, vortex 15 s, briefly centrifuge.

steps.title: Spin‑column binding
steps.instruction: Transfer the lysate to a spin column, avoiding particulate carry‑over, and centrifuge at ≥12 000 × g for 30‑60 s. Discard flow‑through.

steps.title: Column washing – first wash
steps.instruction: Place the column in a new 2 mL collection tube, add 400 µL buffer WB, centrifuge at ≥12 000 × g for 30‑60 s, discard flow‑through.

steps.title: Column washing – ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Transfer column to another fresh 2 mL collection tube, add 400 µL 70 % ethanol, centrifuge at ≥12 000 × g for 3 min, discard flow‑through.

steps.title: DNA elution
steps.instruction: Place the column in a 1.5 mL elution tube, add 30 µL deionized water pre‑heated to 70 °C, incubate 1 min at room temperature, centrifuge at ≥12 000 × g for 1 min, close the tube and store eluted DNA at –80 °C.

steps.title: First PCR setup (ITS1 amplification)
steps.instruction: In a sterile PCR tube (inside a biosafety enclosure), assemble a 21.5 µL reaction: 10 µL 2× GoTaq Green Mastermix (Promega), 0.5 µL forward primer (1 µM, final 0.25 µM), 0.5 µL reverse primer (1 µM, final 0.25 µM), 1.5 µL DNA template, and add nuclease‑free water to volume. Mix gently.

steps.title: First PCR thermocycling
steps.instruction: Run on an Eppendorf 5331 thermal cycler: 95 °C 2 min; 35 cycles of 95 °C 10 s, 48 °C 20 s, 72 °C 10 s; final extension 72 °C 1 min.

steps.title: First PCR product visualization and purification
steps.instruction: Run 2 % agarose gel to confirm amplification, then purify the PCR products using Beckman‑Coulter SPRI beads according to the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Index PCR setup
steps.instruction: Using the purified first‑PCR product as template, set up an index PCR (volumes as per kit instructions) in sterile tubes.

steps.title: Index PCR thermocycling
steps.instruction: Thermocycle: 95 °C 2 min; 8 cycles of 95 °C 10 s, 55 °C 10 s, 72 °C 10 s; final extension 72 °C 30 s.

steps.title: Index PCR product visualization
steps.instruction: Run the indexed amplicons on a gel, visualize bands, and group (aggregate) amplicons according to band intensity.

steps.title: Pooling and bead cleanup
steps.instruction: Pool the aggregated amplicons, then purify the pooled library with SPRI beads at a 0.8 × (v/v) ratio.

steps.title: Library preparation with NEB Ultra II kit
steps.instruction: Process the purified pooled amplicons using the NEB Ultra II Library Preparation Kit (New England Biolabs) following the kit’s instructions; verify expected fragment size on a gel.

steps.title: Library quantification
steps.instruction: Quantify the libraries with Promega Glomax reagent; if a library shows low yield, split samples into two distinct pools with adjusted ratios. Determine final pool concentration using a Denovix high‑sensitivity assay.

steps.title: Sequencing
steps.instruction: Load the final library pool onto an Illumina NovaSEQ 6000 and sequence with 2 × 150 bp paired‑end reads.
